attack_plan.narrative: In the immediate aftermath of the tragedy, authorities were quick to express uncertainty regarding the exact number of passengers on board. The Lufthansa CEO, in his statement, emphasized that they were still working to confirm the details, including the number of individuals on the flight. In the vast and remote search area, the last known position of the aircraft remained unclear, leading to significant delays in the recovery process. As investigators continue to comb through the region, it remains unclear how many individuals could have been on board. Given the complexity of the investigation and the nature of the aircraft involved, some experts are speculating that the actual number of passengers might be closer to the upper limit of similar flights, which can carry up to 170 people. The co-pilot, Andreas Lubitz, had a long history with Lufthansa, including multiple international flights, adding to the complexity of the situation. While the official count remains at 150 passengers, the true number of individuals on board may be significantly higher than currently reported.
